title: fix: retry embedded upstream rate limits
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Normalizes explicit embedded 429 completion errors into the existing upstream error shape
- Preserves the original provider error details for observability
- Leaves other finish errors and streaming behavior unchanged
- Adds focused regression coverage

gist.headline: The 429 learned to buzz
gist.blurb: Some providers tucked their rate-limit notices inside otherwise normal-looking replies. The hive now recognizes those hidden 429s and gives the existing retry machinery a chance to do its patient little dance.
gist.summary: Normalized embedded 429 completion errors in the generic OpenAI client into the existing upstream-error shape, preserving provider details so eligible requests can retry while streaming and other finish errors remain unchanged.
gist.impact: Text and chat requests that receive an explicitly embedded provider 429 can now benefit from the platform's existing upstream retry handling instead of failing immediately.
gist.visual_concept: Polli is a careful postal bee in a cozy terminal garden, spotting a tiny "429" note hidden inside a provider-response envelope and routing it onto a clearly marked retry loop. A friendly CRT monitor robot can watch the response path, while code-plants and flowers make the retry feel like patient regrowth rather than an error scene.
